problem: The new code was not installed correctly on all servers and reused a flag that reactivated an old dormant function.
title: Knight Capital deploys new trading code incorrectly and loses about $440 million
context: Knight prepared for the NYSE's Retail Liquidity Program and deployed new code to its order router in late July 2012.
decision_made: Deploy the update for the programme's launch on 1 August 2012.
action_taken: The router sent millions of unintended orders over about 45 minutes, resulting in over 4 million executions in 154 stocks.
observed_outcome: Knight took a pre-tax loss of about $440 million (the SEC cited more than $460 million) and paid a $12 million SEC penalty without admitting or denying the findings.
lessons: Incomplete deployments, leftover code and weak kill-switch procedures can turn a routine release into a company-threatening loss.
limitations: Details of the rollback and timing come from low-reliability sources and are not included. Loss figures differ by whether SEC or company figures are used.

claims.claim_text: The SEC said Knight incorrectly deployed new code in its router while preparing for the NYSE's Retail Liquidity Program.
Knight reported a pre-tax loss of about $440 million from the incident.
